lab.title: Simulator Lab
lab.intro: Live demos of the simulation engine as it is built. Everything runs in your browser.

scenarioHint.line-follower: Arduino Uno + L298N + two TT motors + 3-channel line sensor on 4×AA. The firmware follows the black line around the oval.
scenarioHint.blink: The Uno toggles D13 every 500 ms through a 220 Ω resistor.
scenarioHint.button: Hold the button: D2 reads LOW through the internal pull-up and the sketch turns the LED on.
scenarioHint.dimmer: Turn the knob: analogRead(A0) sets the PWM duty on D6.
scenarioHint.servo: Turn the knob: the sketch maps A0 to the servo pulse width on D9. The servo runs from its own 4×AA pack — a stalled SG90 needs more than the Uno's 5 V pin can give.
scenarioHint.led-no-resistor: An LED straight on D13 with no resistor. The checker flags it before you run; run it and watch the pin and the LED burn out.
scenarioHint.outputs-fighting: D2 and D3 are wired together; the sketch drives D2 HIGH and D3 LOW — a short circuit through both pins.
scenarioHint.motor-on-pin: A TT motor straight on D9. Motors need a driver: the pin cannot supply the current.
scenarioHint.floating-input: A button on D2 to GND, but the sketch uses INPUT without a pull-up: released, the pin floats.
scenarioHint.serial: The sketch prints a greeting and a tick every second over Serial at 115200 baud, and echoes what you send in capitals (D13 toggles on every byte).
